body.p: This amendment is responsive to the Non-Final Office Action mailed March 20, 2024. Claims 1-10 are pending and stand rejected. Claim 11 has been added.
Claims 1-10 stand rejected on the grounds of nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting as being unpatentable over Claims 1-10 of U.S. Patent 11,772,812.
Without admitting that the double patenting rejection is properly imposed, Applicant is submitting a terminal disclaimer herewith to obviate the double patenting rejection.
In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests that the double patent rejection be withdrawn.
Claim 1 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/025 13 13).

The Office Action states that "Examiner interprets magnets as programmable because they can be in an active state or inactive state and be switched therebetween states: see 029, each electromagnet 106 has a deactivated state in which it does not produce any magnetic force and an activated state in which it produces a magnetic field)"
The Office Action further states that:
[t]herefore, it would have been obvious for one of ordinary skill in the art at the
time of filing the invention to combine the protective cover of Descheemaeker with the
concept of programmable magnets each comprising a single metal piece comprising a

p.u: magnets joined together side-by-side with some of
North-South poles in one direction interspersed with other magnets oriented with

body.p: their South-North poles in the opposite direction, as taught by Gustafsson for the
advantage of have multiple distinct magnetic poles on a single surface, and these multiple
magnetic poles being arranged to form a pattern of north and south poles for customizing
or shaping predetermined magnetic fields.

Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn. The terms "electromagnets" and "programmable magnets" describe fundamentally different types of magnets. See Wikipedia articles on "Programmable magnet" and "Electromagnet".
The magnets described in Descheemaeker are electromagnets, not programmable

magnets. Electromagnets are a type of magnet in which the magnetic field is produced by an electric current. Electromagnets usually consist of a wire wound into a coil. A current through the wire creates a magnetic field which is concentrated in a hole in the center of the coil. The magnetic field disappears when the current is turned off. The main advantage of an electromagnet is that the magnetic field can be quickly changed by controlling the amount of electric current in the winding. An electromagnet requires a continuous supply of current to maintain the magnetic field.
Programmable magnets, on the other hand, are magnetic structures that incorporate
correlated patterns of magnets with alternating polarity, designed to achieve a desired behavior and deliver a stronger local force.
The protective cover described in Descheemaeker will only work if electromagnets are

used. Descheemaeker is intended to provide a protective cover for the wings of an aircraft that is held on by electromagnets and is quickly deployable and retractable using a remote control unit. It would be contrary to the principle of operation of Descheemaeker to use programmable magnets with the protective cover described in Descheemaeker since it would not be possible to selectively turn the magnetic field on and off to deploy and retract the cover.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully requested that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Claims 2-3 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over
Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent
Application 2017/0251313) further in view of Hausmann (U.S. Patent Application 2019/0300199).

Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn. The addition of the Hausmann reference to the combination of the Descheemaeker and Gustafsson references does not cure the deficiencies in the combination of references discussed above in response the rejection of Claim 1. That is, it would be contrary to the principle of operation of Descheemaeker to use programmable magnets with the protective cover described in Descheemaeker since it would not be possible to selectively turn the magnetic field on and off to deploy and retract the cover. The magnet in Hausmann is limited to a single magnet (144) that is configured to interact with a magnetic detector sensor (134) to indicate whether an engine cover (140) is installed on an engine. The magnet in Hausmann is not a programmable magnet, and it is not used to hold the cover to the aircraft. Neither Gustafsson, nor Hausmann provide any teaching or disclosure that enables the protective cover of Descheemaeker to function as intended if it used programmable magnets as suggested in the Office Action.
Therefore, the rejection of Claims 2 and 3 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Claims 4-5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over

Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/0251313) further in view of Hausmann (U.S. Patent Application 2019/0300199) and still further in view of Silver (U.S. Patent Application 2007/0094763).

Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn or the same reasons set forth above in response to the rejection of Claims 2 and 3. That is, it would be contrary to the principle of operation of Descheemaeker to use programmable magnets with the protective cover described in Descheemaeker since it would not be possible to selectively turn the magnetic field on and off to deploy and retract the cover. Silver does not teach or disclose programmable magnets. The Gustafsson, Hausmann, and Silver references do not provide any teaching or disclosure that enables the protective cover of Descheemaeker to function as intended if it used programmable magnets as suggested in the Office Action. Therefore, Silver
does not cure the deficiencies in the combination of the Descheemaeker, Gustafsson and Hausmann references.
Therefore, the rejection of Claims 4 and 5 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claim 6 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/0251313) further in view of Hausmann (U.S. Patent Application 2019/0300199) and still further in view of Silver (U.S. Patent Application 2007/0094763) and still even further in view of Shinotsuka (U.S. Patent Application 2015/0071483).

Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn for the same reasons set forth above in response to the rejection of Claims 4 and 5. That is, it would be contrary to the principle of operation of Descheemaeker to use programmable magnets with the protective cover described in Descheemaeker since it would not be possible to selectively turn the magnetic field on and off to deploy and retract the cover. Shinotsuka also does not teach or disclose an aircraft cover with the programmable magnets as described in Claim 6. Instead, Shinotsuka's permanent magnet has a magnetization pattern of parallel stripes formed such that north pole bands and south pole bands extend in the width direction of the permanent magnet and alternate with each other. Shinotsuka paragraph [0049]. Shinotsuka does not teach or disclose programmable magnets each comprising a single metal piece comprising a plurality of magnets joined together side-by-side with some of said magnets oriented with their North-South poles in one direction interspersed with other magnets oriented with their South-North poles in the opposite direction as described in Claim 1. Shinotsuka, thus, does not cure the deficiencies in the combination of the Descheemaeker, Gustafsson, and Hausmann references.
Therefore, the rejection of Claim 6 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claim 7 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/0251313) further in view of Foo (U.S. Patent Application 2013/0146453).

Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn for the same reasons set forth above in response to the rejection of Claim 1 and for the following additional reasons. Foo is not directed to protecting surfaces as is Descheemaeker. Foo does not disclose any type of cover and, thus, cannot solve the problem with the combination of the Descheemaeker and Gustafsson references. In addition, Foo is directed toward using a magnet pack to shape a magnetic field over a target object in a sputtering process. As stated in paragraph [0002] of Foo, sputtering is a process carried out in a vacuum chamber that is filled with selected gases. The sputtering process causes a substrate (120) to be coated with a material from a target (104) located within a sputtering apparatus. Foo is only concerned with shaping a magnetic field inside a vacuum chamber of a sputtering apparatus. Without the hindsight benefit of having read the Applicant's application, there is nothing in the combination of references that could lead one to conclude that a protective aircraft cover could be created using programmable magnets that are programmed to have a magnetic field strength in a portion different from the magnetic field strength in other portions.
Therefore, the rejection of Claim 7 should be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Claim 8 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/0251313) further in view of Emory (U.S. Patent 5,919,541).

Applicant respectfully requests that this rejection be reconsidered and withdrawn for the same reasons set forth above in response to the rejection of Claim 1 and for the following additional reasons. Emory is directed to a fender cover having a plurality of spaced apart and linearly aligned conventional magnets attached to the fender cover for holding the fender cover to a metal surface. Emory does not teach or disclose programmable magnets as described in Claim 8. The use of conventional magnets described in Emory would also be contrary to the principle of operation of Descheemaeker's protective cover. That is, Emory does not provide any teaching or that would enable the protective cover of Descheemaeker to function as intended if it used programmable magnets as suggested in the Office Action.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully requested that the rejection of Claim 8 be reconsidered and withdrawn.
Claims 9-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over
Descheemaeker (U.S. Patent Application 2020/0039662) in view of Gustafsson (U.S. Patent Application 2017/0251313) further in view of Klein (U.S. Patent 5,267,763).
Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of Claim 9 be reconsidered and

withdrawn or the same reasons set forth above in response to the rejection of Claim 1 and for the following additional reasons. Klein is directed to a vehicle side guard. Klein does not teach or disclose programmable magnets. The use of conventional magnets described in Klein would also be contrary to the principle of operation of Descheemaeker's protective cover. Therefore, Klein does not cure the deficiencies in the combination of the Descheemaeker and Gustafsson references.
Applicant respectfully requests that the rejection of Claim 10 be reconsidered and

withdrawn or the same reasons set forth above in response to the rejection of Claim 9 and for the following additional reason. Descheemaeker discloses an embodiment with only two electromagnets on each wing. Neither Gustafsson nor Klein describe an aircraft. None of the references in the combination of references teaches or discloses the need for not interfering with electronic signals on an aircraft. Without the hindsight benefit of having read the Applicant's application, there is nothing in the combination of references that could lead one to create a protective aircraft cover using programmable magnets that have a magnetic field that does not interfere with electronic signals when installed on an aircraft.
The Office Action also contains a paragraph on the use of a negative limitation in Claim 10. The Office Action states:
In order for the Examiner to give patentable weight to a negative limitation,
Applicant shall provide the reason(s) for the negative limitation to be construed as a
critical element to the invention as a whole, See MPEP 2173.05(i).
The explicit teaching for the negative limitation is found in paragraph [0055] of Applicant's specification where it is stated that:
Use of programmable magnets enables high adherence when in place while not
interfering with electrical equipment that is close by. Programmable magnets can also be
tailored to provide higher strength in one area than another. Conventional magnets
provide field strength at a distance that can interfere with nearby electrical equipment and can damage coatings on the surface of the aircraft if they are used, thus magnets have not
been used previously for covers.
Therefore, the negative limitation should be given patentable weight.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully requested that the rejection of Claims 9 and 10 be reconsidered and withdrawn.

Applicant(s) has made a bona fide effort to respond to each and every requirement set forth in the Office Action. Applicant(s) respectfully believes this case is in condition for allowance and respectfully requests allowance of the pending claims. If the Examiner believes any detailed language of the claims requires further discussion, the Examiner is respectfully asked to telephone the undersigned attorney so that the matter may be promptly resolved. The Examiner's prompt attention to this matter is appreciated.

Applicant(s) is of the opinion that a no fees are due as a result of this Amendment. If any charges or credits are necessary to complete this communication, please apply them to Deposit Account No. AF 01-0465.
Respectfully submitted,
